units.source_text: But one of her ideas fits what I’m trying to say: when two people come together, something appears between them that is larger than either person alone. She calls it the spirit of the relationship.
units.output_text: Well, one of the things she said that is relevant here is that the spirit of the relationship is bigger than the two of them.

units.source_text: I don’t think that spirit belongs to us. Nobody can command it to remain.
units.output_text: The spirit of the relationship doesn’t belong to them; they can’t command it to stay with them.

units.source_text: At our best, we serve it. We tell the truth, keep doing our own inner play & work (pl/ork), ask the community for help, and listen for what the relationship is becoming.
units.output_text: At best they can serve it by telling the truth, engaging in their own play & work (pl/ork), seeking help from their community, etc.

units.source_text: When we start thinking we own it or deserve it, that presumptuousness tends to push it away.
units.output_text: But if they are presumptuous enough to think that they either own it or deserve it, then it will likely go away.
